# Originary

Originary helps teams issue and verify portable signed records for machine actions.
Current protocol release: PEAC v0.16.2, which adds evidence patterns for paid resources, paid MCP tool records, linked counterparty acknowledgments, Merkle commitment helpers, external evidence anchoring, agent spend attribution, agent run lineage records, consented action records, and runtime lineage exports. The wire format is unchanged.

Last updated: 2026-07-08

Company: Poem, Inc.
Location: Delaware, USA
Contact: contact@originary.xyz

## What it is

Portable verification for API, MCP, agent, gateway, payment, and provisioning workflows.

Originary helps teams create signed records so another party can verify what happened without internal logs, dashboard access, or vendor runtime.

## Product pages

- https://www.originary.xyz/how-it-works - how signed records are issued at six surfaces (API, MCP, agent, gateway, payment, provisioning) and verified offline
- https://www.originary.xyz/records - gallery of signed record types (API, MCP, agent, gateway, payment, provisioning), each verifiable offline
- https://www.originary.xyz/verify - verify a signed record by its issuer's public key; offline by design, nothing stored
- https://www.originary.xyz/mcp - signed records for MCP tool calls, gateway decisions, and result digests
- https://www.originary.xyz/ai-gateway - signed records for AI gateway decisions: allow, deny, redaction digests, and observed spend
- https://www.originary.xyz/provisioning-records - signed records for deployments, provider setup, credentials, budgets, and resource lifecycle events
- https://www.originary.xyz/agentic-commerce - signed records that prove what a paid agent action was for

## Open protocol

PEAC Protocol is open-source software for portable signed interaction records, published and maintained by Originary.

- https://github.com/peacprotocol/peac

## Notes

Originary does not replace gateways, observability, payment rails, policy engines, or runtimes. It records selected facts so another party can verify what happened later.
